draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Bijapur! This was the capital of the Adil Shahi sultans, and their Gol Gumbaz has the second-largest dome in the world. Up in its whispering gallery, you can hear a watch tick from the other side of the dome, more than 200 feet away.
draft.hungryLine: The sights are spread around the old citadel, so grab a meal in town between monuments and keep water handy.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Gagan Mahal is a 5 min walk and the unfinished Bara Kaman is 6 minutes away. Jod Gumbaz is about a 10 min walk, and Gol Gumbaz sits on Station Road.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Hang out on the open lawns of the restored Gagan Mahal, where locals and visitors come to sit and chat.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Malik-E-Maidan, the giant cannon on the fort wall, is 4.45 m long and the largest surviving piece of medieval artillery.

spots.name: Gagan Mahal
spots.detail: 5 min walk · Ali Adil Shah I's 1561 palace of the skies, now beautifully restored

spots.name: Bara Kaman
spots.detail: 6 min walk · The unfinished tomb of Ali Adil Shah II and his family

spots.name: Jod Gumbaz
spots.detail: 10 min walk · Twin tombs, still an active dargah

legends.title: The shadow that never fell
legends.body: Rumour has it Bara Kaman was left unfinished because, once complete, its shadow would have touched the Gol Gumbaz. Only two of its planned arches ever went up vertically.

tips.title: Go to Gol Gumbaz early.
tips.body: It's open 06:00 to 18:00, and an early visit lets you try the whispering gallery before the crowds.

tips.title: Take the 8-site tour.
tips.body: Autos and tongas offer a package tour of the big eight sites, and drivers carry a leaflet describing each one.

story.title: City of victory
story.body: The city was founded under the Kalyani Chalukyas and called Vijayapura, city of victory. It passed to the Yadavas after the Chalukyas.

story.title: The sultans arrive
story.body: The Bahmani Sultanate conquered the area. When it split, the Bijapur Sultanate of the Adil Shahis ruled from here.

story.title: Palace and cannon
story.body: Ali Adil Shah I built the Gagan Mahal in 1561. In 1565 the great cannon Malik-E-Maidan helped Bijapur defeat the Vijayanagar empire at Talikot.

story.title: A stepwell for a queen
story.body: Ibrahim Adil Shah II built the Taj Bawdi stepwell in 1620 for his wife, Queen Taj Sultana. His own tomb, Ibrahim Rauza, followed in 1626.

story.title: Gol Gumbaz
story.body: Gol Gumbaz was built as the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah and his family. It's still the largest unsupported dome in the world.
